name: pulley-roof stone well
label: workshop-objectgen-3/c7-well
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (4/4)

surfaces.part: well mouth with water inside, stone rim around it

answer.evidence: The well body is a stone drum. Rows 25-34 show a rim that narrows at the back (width 16 at row 25, then 24-28). Teal water is visible inside the opening at rows 27-33, which is evidence (d). A light front rim line at about row 34 separates it from the brick front face at rows 35-47, which is about 12 rows. The pulley roof at rows 1-13 is a sloped plank plane with a dark eave line at rows 12-13, which is evidence (c). The posts are thin vertical supports. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The closest reference, prop-well-roofed, shows 20 visible tones per 16x16 tile and 38 distinct colours in total. The candidate shows only 5 visible tones per tile and 14 colours in total, so it is much lower on the primary density fact. By eye, the stone body is built from a few grey-blue values with simple block seams. The reference shades its stones one by one and adds moss and water detail. The candidate's roof is a brown plank block with only 2-3 steps and no per-tile highlights or scallops. Its dark edges are 43% near-neutral, so the outline is mixed: partly tinted, partly a flat dark line. That leans toward the sticker look next to the reference's tinted outlines. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills, but the small tone count shows shallow shading and thin texture. A careful artist would see it as flatter and less rich than the reference well beside it.

surfaces.part: stone well rim with water opening

answer.evidence: The stone well body is rows 25-47. Its top is rows 25-34: a back rim at 25-27, teal water visible inside the opening at about rows 27-32, and a light front rim band ending at row 34. Below that is a stone brick front face of about 13 rows (35-47). The plank roof (rows 1-13) is a sloped plane with stepped width growth and a dark eave line at row 13. The posts and pulley are thin vertical supports. The well shows an open container with water seen from above and a front face, so it reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The closest reference, prop-well-roofed, shows 20 visible tones per 16x16 tile and 38 distinct colours. The candidate shows only 5 visible tones per tile and 14 colours in total, even though it is drawn larger. Its stone body and wooden roof each read as about 3 steps: a base tone, a darker joint or line, and a light edge. The reference has per-stone shading, roof-plank highlights and a layered water basin. The candidate has no flat 5x5 blocks (0%), so it is not flat-filled. Its grey brick pattern and plank lines are only sparse texture, with no per-stone variation or grain. Dark edge pixels are 43% neutral, so the outline is partly neutral dark and partly tinted, which I call mixed. That is not the dark-material-tone outlining the reference uses. Overall it looks thinner and more sticker-like than prop-well-roofed beside it.

surfaces.part: well basin top with rim and water opening

answer.evidence: The well basin has a stone rim with a dark teal water area visible inside the opening (rows 28-33, evidence d). A light front-edge line at about row 34 sits above the stone block front face (rows 35-47, 13 rows). The sloped shingle roof (rows 1-13) is a roof plane with its own top surface. The posts are thin vertical supports, which is acceptable. The bucket sits in the opening and counts as decor.

styleAnswer.evidence: The closest reference, prop-well-roofed, has 20 visible tones per tile and 38 colours in total. The candidate has 5 visible tones per tile and only 14 colours in total, so it is far below the same-kind reference. The roof and stone body use roughly 3 lightness steps each, against about 5-6 in the reference, and the roof planks and stone blocks are drawn with simple lines rather than per-tile or per-stone highlights. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills, but that comes from sparse line work rather than rich grain. Dark edge pixels are 43% neutral, so the outline is partly near-black and partly tinted, which I call mixed. This is the flatter, more sticker-like version of the reference well, so it fails.

surfaces.part: well basin opening with water and stone rim
wooden posts and crossbeam with pulley

answer.evidence: The main body is the stone well basin. Rows 25-27 are the back rim and rows 28-33 show dark teal water with highlights inside the opening, which is evidence (d). A light front rim line at about rows 34-35 follows, then the stone-brick front face on rows 36-47, about 12 rows. The silhouette is not an ellipse (width goes 16, 24, 26, 28), but the visible water contents count as a top surface. The shingled roof on rows 1-13 is a sloped plane (c) with a dark eave line on row 13. The posts are thin supports and do not need tops.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is the same kind as prop-well-roofed, but it is much thinner in craft. It has only 5 visible tones per 16x16 tile against 20 for the roofed-well reference, and only 14 distinct colours in total against 38. Each material ramp (the brown roof and posts, the grey stone, the dark water) shows about 3 steps, where Beodeul uses 5-6. The roof reads as a few plank bands with little per-plank grain or highlight. The stone courses are regular and lightly shaded, with little stone-by-stone variation. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills, and the bricks and planks give some texture, but it is simpler than the reference. 43% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is mixed: part dark-material tone and part greyish dark line, which gives a slight sticker feel. Taken together, the piece is cleanly drawn but shallower than the reference and would look flatter beside it.
